source_basis: Own complete hash-identical model-visible 2018FAQ/history/question07 readings, own current10 reconstruction and ledgers, and complete newly delivered delta10-to12. No peer outputs or summary/key information.

whole_faq_history_current_bank_stratum_v.statement: The census indexes clauses and direct quotations from every one of407 FAQ Q/A units, individual standalone errata, all94 historical Q/A units and retained errata, with each literal original-alien/flare/artifact mention linked to seven-axis checks. Current Q104/Q166 now ask the previously proposed Super boundaries and Fido acquisition. The remaining qualifying branch is Machine Wild’s guaranteed second encounter after an unsuccessful first; Q121 uses the guarantee as a given and tests replacement instead. Ordinary-only Planning remains unadopted, and the four held human choices remain pending. This is a source-stratum closure challenge, not a new vote or global PASS.

current_binding.canonicalization: Complete question object, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators comma/colon, UTF8 SHA256.

census_method.unit_scope: All407 FAQ QA + individually split standalone errata; all94 historical QA + six retained/base erratum groups. Questions, answers, examples, direct quotations and independently operative nested clauses are retained distinctly.
census_method.fragment_index: Exact source-character spans and hashes for sentence/operational clauses plus separate direct-quotation subfragments. Splitting creates an audit checklist, not automatic new-candidate counts.
guardrails: A source question given is not automatically an actual asked fact in the bank.
A direct quote may support its bounded clause while full roles/effects/timing remain genuinely unprovided.
A paragraph reference or alien name never gives coverage to every neighboring statement.
Initial-placement windows are not inferred from when-effect-works wording.
Miser start-of-each-own-encounter is not equated to once-per-turn StartTurn.
Excluded examples remain excluded even when they mention base aliens.
Repeated constants/names or already-tested operator combinations do not generate new candidates.
census_method.historical_handling: Changed old answers remain superseded by 2018; retained Macron/Spiff/Warrior/MindWild/ReincarnatorWild errata remain. No native cached-PDF availability/hash is claimed.
census_method.exact_historical_locators: Every historical clause now carries its exact starting/ending cached L labels as well as source-character span and chunk hash. Concatenated Q labels are preserved by character offsets.

operative_quotes: Machine Wild guarantees the player a second encounter
you may always have a second encounter
accepted_new_candidates.proposed_literal_question: Assume Machine Wild is otherwise legally played and the game is still continuing. Does its FAQ-described guarantee of a second encounter require the first encounter to have been successful, or can it grant the second encounter after an unsuccessful first encounter?
minimal_source_backed_required_facts: The FAQ-described Machine Wild guarantee can grant a second encounter despite an unsuccessful first; it is not restricted to the ordinary success prerequisite.
accepted_new_candidates.positive_original_base_application: Machine Wild is an original-base flare expressly described by the official FAQ. An ordinary unsuccessful first encounter is reachable with original attack/negotiate outcomes. The guarantee/always clause is a direct operative statement and needs no expansion or Technology; otherwise-legal play and an ongoing game are supplied, without inventing full printed role or placement timing.

actual_asked_overlap.literal_question: After a successful first encounter may offense start a second with no encounter card, hoping to obtain one later? What ends an ordinary turn after first or second encounter?

For Machine, state the eligible player role, whether use is optional or mandatory, and its phase(s); then explain after what outcomes may Continuity grant another encounter, how many encounters may its turn contain and what hand requirement remains?

After being played once, do Anti-Matter Super, Cudgel Super, Kamikaze Super, Machine Super, Masochist Super, Miser Super, or Machine Wild automatically apply in later encounters, or must the corresponding flare be played again each encounter its effect is desired? For otherwise legal uses, what timing phrases does the official FAQ quote for the effects of Kamikaze Super, Machine Super, Masochist Super, Miser Super and Cudgel Super? For the first three, does the quoted wording refer to every player's Regroup or to the user's own Regroup phases?
When Machine Wild guarantees a second encounter but the player needs a new hand to take it, what happens to the old hand and to the Machine flare during the replacement?

accepted_new_candidates.meaningful_novelty: Q121 assumes the guarantee as context and asks what happens to the old hand and flare during replacement; it never asks whether a failed first encounter qualifies. Q104 now asks replay and the specified Super timing phrases, not this Wild outcome exception. Q017 asks ordinary second-encounter prerequisites, and Q041 is Machine’s distinct alien-sheet power. A correct answer to all four can still omit or deny this specific Wild exception after first-encounter failure. This is an outcome/eligibility branch rather than another acquisition or arithmetic example.
limits: No third encounter, post-victory continuation, complete role/trigger/phase/initial-placement window, full flare text or new-hand quantity is inferred.
Q121 already tests replacement and return, so those facts are not counted again.

rejected_candidate_additions.operative_quote: Is a planet with a space station, citadel, saboteur token, etc. still considered empty if there are no ships on it?
rejected_candidate_additions.positive_base_only_enabler: Original Citadel can leave a citadel on a planet without ships; the general answer says yes. Pack Rat collecting the planet is excluded.
rejected_candidate_additions.consequential_novelty: The relevant occupancy test remains absence of ships, already exercised by the colony definition and empty-home reclamation. Persistent citadels already have their own facedown/discard outcome question. A separate no-ships-plus-marker example adds no independent colony or reclamation mechanic.

rejected_candidate_additions.operative_quote: Ships land on colonies simultaneously (e.g., when released from the warp after a Mobius Tubes)
rejected_candidate_additions.positive_base_only_enabler: Mobius Tubes releasing base ships to existing colonies is explicitly named by the primary FAQ.
rejected_candidate_additions.consequential_novelty: Q156 directly asks simultaneous versus one-at-a-time landing. The extra requirement to commit ships before Saboteur reveals a token depends on excluded Saboteur; no new base trap/test landing is justified.

rejected_candidate_additions.operative_quote: You must declare all of your reward sources before taking them.
rejected_candidate_additions.positive_base_only_enabler: Base successful defensive ally may choose cosmic cards and warp ships as rewards.
rejected_candidate_additions.consequential_novelty: Q155 explicitly asks whether a first reward card can be inspected before deciding remaining sources and when to commit the full mix. No abstract duplicate is needed.

Would be a distinct destiny redraw branch if reachable. These sources establish no positive original-base effect making all five such colonies exist before ordinary victory. Do not reuse Q086 or count hypothetical post-victory play.
Omega Missile/Locust are excluded; a base color name cannot supply a planet destruction mechanism.
Black Hole is excluded. Without a positive base unowned competing effect, adding its final timing slot does not create a reachable original-base test.

Allowed sources do not identify an original-base sheet-theft enabler. Lending Miser and temporary Reincarnator Super prohibition are already concrete applications; do not invent base Plant/Changeling.

rejected_candidate_additions.rationale: Replay-each-encounter examples duplicate Q104/Q123/Q148. Current12 Q104 also now explicitly asks the quoted Super timing/owner phrases; no additional name-by-name replay or timing question is needed.

rejected_candidate_additions.positive_base_only_enabler: Vacuum Super with original Zombie colonies, explicitly described in primary FAQ.
rejected_candidate_additions.consequential_novelty: Q134 already tests losing simultaneous single-ship colonies and inability to relocate among them; a second arithmetic or color variant repeats it.

Token means ship supplies terminology only. No full original Gambler Super effect, new costs, or abilities can be reconstructed from its name. This limitation also applies to any flare/artifact not given operative primary effect text in these allowed sources.

rejected_candidate_additions.positive_base_only_enabler: The primary FAQ expressly quotes original Mite Super’s acquisition clause.
rejected_candidate_additions.rationale: Q162 now asks encounter-only versus any original-base type, concretely including an artifact. A different original card type is a mechanical variant. It does not establish or require the absent full trigger/role/phase/cost/duration.

The excerpt establishes the acquisition wording and discusses reward-pile immediate interception. It does not give the full original Mite Super trigger, role, cost or duration. Do not infer full activation eligibility or a free later search of the original discard pile from the name or quoted clause. The excluded reward-pile later-retrieval distinction is not a new original-base branch.

Q163 explicitly tests the full procedure given in this example: mixed hands, random acquisition, and flare outside the mixture then returned. No additional selective-versus-random, keep-separate, or return-order example adds a rule.

Do not infer which player may invoke Oracle Wild when, which opponent must be selected, numerical hand sizes or allocation rules not written in this example. Q163 earns only the expressly asked example components.

The FAQ quotes when the effect works, not the complete rules for placing the flare earlier or its full benefit. The accepted timing question preserves only whenever you use your power. A novel claim about preemptive placement, damage quantity or other full effect would need unseen native text.
During each encounter establishes replay context already tested by Q104; it does not state a new precise phase, role or effect from which to construct another consequential question.

The actual affirmative example and timing conflict require excluded Warhawk. Its general Timing Rules component is already Q019.
